#3701. Grand Theft Auto 6 becomes the most pre-ordered game in PlayStation Store history

Sony has just announced that Grand Theft Auto 6 has become "the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store". Note, it's not the most pre-ordered game in PlayStation history, just on its digital PlayStation Store.

The announcement, which comes as Sony prepares to ditch physical releases for an all-digital future, was made in a PlayStation Blog post confirming pre-loads for GTA 6 are now live.

"Grand Theft Auto 6 is now the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store," Sony wrote. "Given this unprecedented demand, we've joined with Rockstar Games to allow players to start pre-loading the game nine days early, so they're ready to play on launch day.

"We strongly advise that everyone who is hoping to play on launch day to pre-load the game as soon as possible," the blog post added. So: consider yourselves advised.

GTA 6 becomes available as soon as your region's clock ticks over from midnight into 19th November, which, if you're in New Zealand, means you'll play the game before everyone else. If only there were a way to pretend you lived there...

Elsewhere in the blog post, Sony underlined some features coming specially to GTA 6 on PS5 and PS5 Pro. On Xbox, meanwhile, cloud streaming is supported, but not - sadly - to PC.

Last night, in a Take-Two financial earnings call, company leader Strauss Zelnick said pre-orders for GTA 6 are tracking "far above expectations" and that soon, "numbers will speak for themselves". Presumably because they will be gripped by an excited form of sentience. It's expected that GTA 6 could become the best-selling instalment in an already mega-selling series; Zelnick reckons GTA 6 will "set a new baseline" for Take-Two in terms of success.

Have you managed to resist pre-ordering it yet?

#3700. What’s It Really Like For Bari Weiss To Run CBS News? She Shared Some Honest Thoughts

Managing such a brand is no walk in the park.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Bari Weiss has been the editor-in-chief of CBS News for over a year now, and her tenure has been quite eventful. For months, media analysts have weighed in on Weiss’ direction of the company and, while she’s received praise in some circles, she’s also received backlash. Of course, running a media corporation is no small feat and, just recently, Weiss was asked about what it’s really been like for her to hold down the big job. With that, the veteran journalist shared some candid thoughts about the inner workings of the brand.

For the most part, it’s rare that Weiss sits down to discuss her role at CBS in depth, and she did just that during a recent discussion held by The Information at the WTF Summit. Weiss discussed a number of topics amid the conversation (which can be seen on YouTube), including concerns about 60 Minutes’ low ratings and the notion of her running CNN someday. Host Jessica Lessin asked Weiss about the practicalities of running a news outlet, leading the E-I-C to make some quick jokes:

I don't work out. I don't sleep. I don't have any friends left. I mean, that would be one answer to that question.

After sharing those quips, though, Weiss got serious quite quickly, saying the experience had been “consuming.” Lessin went on to make note of CBS News’ position within the pantheon of legacy news outlets and how old-school principles may work against Weiss’ vision for the brand. While Weiss mentioned that there had been success within the company, she also spoke to some of the challenges facing it:

I would say on the inside, it's been tremendously successful. The disparity — I mean, I'm sure you all work at places that are covered and scrutinized. You know that the gap between the stories that are being told and the actual experience of it in the case of CBS, it's like a chasm. If I spent all of my time being concerned about trying to tell a different story, I would not be able to run the actual news organization.

One Of Bari Weiss’ New 60 Minutes Stars Has Blunt Advice For CBS News Staffers Amid Backlash

One of the key points of discussion that has surrounded Bari Weiss since David Ellison hired her involves her editorial prowess. Some of her choices have come under fire, including her last-minute decision to cut a 60 Minutes story about the Terrorism Confinement Center in El Salvador almost a year ago. At the time, Weiss concluded that more research needed to be done before the story could go to air. Weiss has still, however, been accused of initiating “journalistic interference,” and journalists like Dan Rather and Scott Pelley have criticized her leadership abilities, particularly due to her lack of broadcast journalism experience prior to CBS.

However, CBS Evening News anchor Tony Dokoupil spoke positively about Weiss’ vision and said he hadn’t witnessed any news bias. Newly hired correspondent Sir Trevor Phillips also defended Weiss and her approach to putting together a team of journalists. Regardless of praise or criticism, though, Weiss emphasized during the interview that she had been aiming to tune out noise. She now seems to be looking ahead to the future, and she explained her intention to create change in an ever-evolving media landscape:

This is one of the most storied important news organizations in the world. It was built for a time where there were three news channels that you could choose from on the television. We now live in a world of infinite information, choice and possibility. By necessity, that means it has to change. Every single legacy news organization has to change, because we're in — the attention, whatever you want to call it, we are in a a fierce competition to get people to command people's attention to make sure that [what] we are offering them is something that matters.

Bari Weiss went on to say “the change that's required is painful as it would be in any organization that has to change the way it does business.” It is indeed true that the industry has been experiencing growing pains as of late as the overall media model undergoes alterations. While we can’t say just how CBS News will fit into that framework moving forward, Weiss seems keen on running the brand in a way that’s fluid and viable.

#3699. It’s A Relief To Go Back To The Simple Joy Of Ocarina Of Time After A Decade Of Being Overwhelmed By Breath Of The Wild

The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the WildThe Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of TimeThe Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom

My friends, put the tomatoes down. I havenât even gotten to speak yet. I, like most people who own a Nintendo Switch 2 and are killing time until Grand Theft Auto 6 launches next week, am playing The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, and Iâm having a pretty good time going back to a game that was once an elementary school obsession for me, especially because itâs been a long time since I really felt a constant sense of progression in a Zelda game after a decade of Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom.

Yeah, the game is incredibly simple by modern standards, and Nintendo has done a lot to ensure that by making the game demonstrably easier in dozens of small ways that add up, but I think that relative simplicity is what draws me to it. Iâve been chipping away at the game in short sessions, usually finishing a temple or two before putting it down for the rest of the day, and the tangible feeling of momentum is what keeps me coming back to it just about every other evening at this point.

Over the years, especially with the rise of open-world games, I have identified that I am a goal-oriented person when it comes to how a video game can hold my attention. Thereâs just so much competition for whatever spare hours I have that if the bulk of my time playing a game is spent getting to the things I care about, I can lose interest fairly quickly. I want to see where the story goes, I want to reach the end of a quest line, and I loathe tedious open-world traversal more than most video game activities.Â

I canât entirely avoid open-world games in 2026, but if a game doesnât have a quick or engaging way to get around a giant map, it actively deters me from playing it. I often cite the Infamous series, with all its superpowered movement and interesting environmental interactions, as a great example of a game that makes its open-world map tolerable to me. A car or a horse is probably not going to cut it. There are exceptions from time to time, such as Cyberpunk 2077âs Night City entrancing me so much that Iâd gladly take in the view as I drove around on my motorcycle. But if I can help it, I want to spend my limited gaming time on things that arenât simply moving from one side of a giant space to another.

Breath of the Wild and its excellent sequel, Tears of the Kingdom do a lot to break up the tedium of simply moving through a space. The survival sim-esque friction and gizmo-building mechanics are brilliant evolutions of the original Zelda formula, and Nintendoâs ability to still draw water from the well of a decades-old franchise is commendable. I really enjoyed my time with both games, despite them grinding against a lot of my ingrained gaming sensibilities. The puzzles in the shrines, the constant feeling of discovery in its giant open world, and the colorful casts of weirdos and heroes you meet throughout the games maintain all that same Zelda spirit, but with a meaningful expansion of what a Zelda game looks like.Â

But man, is it a relief to go back to Ocarina of Time. I want puzzle-solving and discovery that I can get to quickly, that doesnât need me to meaningfully prep a survival bag so I can trek to the other side of the map while hoping my melee weapons can last me the whole trip, and what Ocarina is delivering feels downright breezy. Iâm sorry, Iâm sorry. I know itâs regressive of me to say Iâd like for the series to strip away all the cool things itâs done in the past nine years, but I havenât had a Zelda experience that feels like this in so long. The top-down 2D games are similar (at least those that came after the pretty open-ended and opaque original game), but they donât have the targeting and swordplay of the postâOcarina of Time era that rounds out the vision I have of what makes a 3D Zelda game.

I donât really hold any illusions that Zelda is going to go back to the structure of Ocarina of Time, but it is refreshing to be handed the tools I need to accomplish things without worrying that my weapon is going to break from battle damage or that Iâll run out of some vital consumable before I reach my goal. The Legend of Zelda is gonna be fine no matter where it goes moving forward, but for as dated and small in scope as Ocarina of Time might feel compared to Tears of the Kingdom, it sure does remind me that there was once a time when I didnât feel like I was fighting against the elements just to get to where I wanted to go.

#3698. Here's our second wave of PS Plus games for November 2026 - and Sony's scrapping its barely used PC app

Death Stranding 2! Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii! Atomfall!

Sony's revealed the second wave of games coming to PlayStation Plus Premium and Extra this month, and there are some genuine big-name attractions, led by Hideo Kojima's futuristic delivery man showstopper Death Stranding 2: On the Beach.

Here's the new games coming PlayStation Plus Extra and Premium in November:

And here are a couple of games coming only to PlayStation Plus Premium in November:

There's a lot to recommend in that list. Death Stranding 2 was one of the standout games of 2025. "A busier, louder, and more emotionally resplendent take on this singular hiking sim," Lewis Gordon wrote in Eurogamer's Death Stranding 2 review.

Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii also shone brightly last year, as ridiculous as it was. "A raucous, absurd spin-off that manages to still feel like a first-rate Yakuza game despite the leftfield setting and delightfully unhinged plot," wrote Matt Elliott in Eurogamer's Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii review.

Meanwhile, Atomfall - Rebellion's quirky British take on a Fallout-like post-apocalyptic idea - was awarded three out of five stars. "If you can get over a difficult start and fancy a lean take on the survival genre, Atomfall delivers an intriguing tale worth discovering," Tom Orry wrote in Eurogamer's Atomfall review. It's presumably been significantly patched and smoothed since then.

The Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D Remake also scored three out of five stars. "Some excellent enhancements make this the ultimate version of Dragon Quest 3, but it could still do more to make it wholly welcoming to newcomers," Daniella Lucas wrote in Eurogamer's Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D review.

We didn't review Hell Let Loose, but the popular World War 2 shooter would go on to amass a serious following and spawn a follow-up game in Hell Let Loose: Vietnam recently, which we did review. "The lavish jungles, rigid command structure, and emphasis on communication make Hell Let Loose: Vietnam a fascinating war simulator when it works. But its many variables can all too easily devolve into a miserable snipe-fest," Rick Lane wrote.

There's plenty to be getting on with, then.

Sony also announced in the PlayStation Blog post it's retiring the PS Plus app on PC from 10th December. Why? Because nobody really uses it.

"With a very small number of eligible PlayStation Plus Premium members (less than 0.4 percent) using the PlayStation Plus app on PC, making this change allows us to focus on enhancing high-quality experiences that more of our members want to use," Sony wrote. "As a result, the PlayStation Plus cloud streaming app on PC will no longer be available."

For more information on PlayStation Plus, you can check out our guide to PS Plus and all the available games here.

Yes, this fits with Sony's broader pullback from PC, but the real reason the app is "retiring" is a simple lack of interest.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Sony took another step back from the PC today, announcing that the PlayStation Plus app for PC will be "retiring" on December 10. I can't really blame it for this one, though: Almost nobody was actually using it.

"PlayStation believes in providing high-quality experiences to our players, and we regularly review offerings to ensure we are focusing on experiences our members value most," Sony wrote at the tail-end of a PlayStation Blog update detailing the PlayStation Plus game lineup for November.

"With a very small number of eligible PlayStation Plus Premium members (less than 0.4%) using the PlayStation Plus app on PC, making this change allows us to focus on enhancing high-quality experiences that more of our members want to use. As a result, the PlayStation Plus cloud streaming app on PC will no longer be available."

The end of the app seems to fit pretty well with Sony's recent about-face on PC gaming: After a brief period of enthusiasm for bringing its big exclusives to PC, Sony began a walkback earlier this year, shifting its focus back to consoles exclusives. It hasn't explicitly acknowledged or explained the change in strategy, but as PC Gamer's Morgan Park wrote in May, the thing speaks for itself: Rather like Xbox "recommitting" to its console, "Sony is responding to a waning interest in consoles by reinforcing its 'narrative singleplayer games' as system sellers once again.

"Multiplayer games like the upcoming Marvel Tōkon will still come to PC, but if you want to play the next prestige action game from the likes of Naughty Dog or Insomniac, you'll need a PS5," Morgan wrote. Or, when the time comes, a PlayStation 6.

Similar to Xbox cloud streaming, the PlayStation Plus app on PC was really more noteworthy for the selection of older PlayStation games it offered to PC gamers, rather than major new releases. Given that, I think the end has come for exactly the reason Sony cited: Not due to any strategic realignment, but simply because nobody's using it in the first place.

#3696. PlayStation Cancels Fairgames After Years Of Silence

Another one of PlayStation’s live-service games has crashed and burned, asÂ Fairgames, the company’s online shooter that was being developed by first-party PlayStation developer Haven Studios, has been canceled.

As reported by Bloomberg, Haven Studios isn’t undergoing any layoffs as a result of the cancelation, as “the studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities,” according to a statement provided to the publication by PlayStation. The decision comes after Fairgames‘ recent playtest didn’t live up to Sony’s internal expectations.

âWhile the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,â PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle wrote in an email to employees and verified by Bloomberg. âCombined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.â

FairgamesÂ was initially announced back in 2023, and was originally being led by Jade Raymond, known as a producer of the earlyÂ Assassin’s Creed games. Raymond left Haven Studios in 2025, though the project quietly continued development. We really haven’t heard much about the game since it was initially unveiled.

Haven Studios was initially founded in 2021, and Sony acquired the company in 2022 before it had even put out a game. Now, it sounds like those who had been working onÂ FairgamesÂ will support the development of other games by PlayStation studios.

Fairgames is the latest in a long line of live-service disasters for Sony as the company continues to greenlight and then cancel its various attempts at forever games. Perhaps most famously, the company removed multiplayer shooter Concord from storefronts and then subsequently shut down its developer, Firewalk Studios.

Despite all this, Sony is still adamant that live-service games are an important part of PlayStation’s future.

Mean Girls is arguably one of the best movies of the 2000s, and it’s no surprise fans continue to support the film that launched a mini franchise with a sequel, a musical reboot released in 2024, and a Tony-nominated musical. The talented movie cast has gone on to do amazing things, which has kept them mostly apart until now. For the first time in a long time, Lindsay Lohan reunited with some of her Mean Girls cast on the set of her newest film, Return to You, and I’m not the only one obsessed with the photos.

Lohan, who famously played Cady Heron in the 2004 flick, has been filming an upcoming Netflix film alongside Mean Girls director Mark Waters. Last month, Waters revealed the film was filming at an iconic Mean Girls location, and now it seems they’ve tapped some of the cast to join them in this walk down memory lane. Waters once again took to his Instagram to share the photos of the mini reunion with Sharron Matthews, Stefanie Drummond, and Daniel DeSanto:

A post shared by Mark Waters (@mark_s_waters)

For those who might need a refresher, Waters also included photos of Matthews, Drummond, and DeSanto as their Mean Girls characters Joan (a teacher), Bethany (a fellow high school student), and Jason (Gretchen’s on-again, off-again boyfriend). It’s so heartwarming seeing them reunite, and I’m not the only one who thinks so. Fellow Mean Girls actor Jonathan Bennett, who played Aaron Samuels, was quick to comment on the post, writing:

As much as I would love to see the Freakier Friday actress reunite with “The Plastics” in another movie, I’m obsessed with the fact that Waters and Lohan, who is also producing the project, chose to include some of the iconic but lesser-known actors from the film. It also makes sense since Return to You is set to take place in the noughties, 2008 to be exact.

Lohan will play a lonely attorney who has been accidentally sent an emotional DVD from a dying woman addressed to the woman’s husband (played by Henry Golding). While it’s unclear what role the trio will play in the Netflix rom-com, the photos do give us some clues. DeSanto is definitely going to be a lawyer of some sort; whether that be a coworker or an enemy remains to be seen. Matthews can be seen in an office setting, which makes me think she could be a potential client. Drummond looks like she’s in a home, so maybe she plays a sister or mother of the dying woman.

Of course, all of this is purely speculation at this point. With production of the romance film just starting, it’s going to be a while before Return to You is available for those with a Netflix subscription, but that also means that there’s time for even more Mean Girls references and cameos to make an appearance in the film. Until then, fans can stream Mean Girls with an active Paramount+ subscription.

#3694. You Can Play GTA 6 On A 13-Year-Old Xbox And It’ll Run At The Same Framerate As PS5 Pro

GTA 6PS5 ProXbox Cloud GamingXbox Series X/S

Grand Theft Auto 6 is only coming to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S at launch, but that doesn’t mean those consoles will be the only places to play it. Technically, fans who are still on Xbox One, which came out back in 2013, will also have a shot at exploring Rockstar Games’ latest version of Vice City thanks to Xbox Cloud Gaming.

Microsoft revealed the surprise last-gen perk in an update to its cloud gaming program this week. “Grand Theft Auto VI will be playable on day one through Xbox Cloud Gaming on Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S, starting at 1am ET,” the company announced. “That means more players can experience one of the most anticipated games of the year on the consoles they already own. The game uses Xbox Series S graphics settings when cloud-streamed with Xbox Cloud Gaming.”

Series S graphics settings include the game running at a targeted 30fps framerate, the same as what will be available to players on Xbox Series X and PS5, as well as PS5 Pro. Sony’s more powerful hardware will still give players access to improved image quality with PSSR, but the game won’t run at 60fps anywhere, at least not at launch.

So what do you need in order to play GTA 6 on an Xbox One? Well, you’ll still need to own a digital copy of the game, which costs $80 and began pre-loading this week. You’ll also need access to Xbox Cloud Gaming, either via a Game Pass subscription or via Ã  la carte pricing. Ten hours of cloud gaming time in Vice City will cost Xbox owners $4.

What you won’t be able to do is stream GTA 6 to a mobile device or PC. Those options, which are a standard part of the rest of Xbox Cloud Gaming’s offerings, are excluded from the streaming agreement with Rockstar. It’s unclear if that’s a functionality that may be added sometime down the road after the game has been out for a while. GTA 6 will also support remote play on both Xbox and PS5, meaning you can stream it to other screens locally, including the PS Portal.

“Weâre excited to bring Grand Theft Auto 6 to more Xbox players at launch, and we will also be adding more titles from Rockstar Games to Xbox Cloud Gaming including Grand Theft Auto 5, Red Dead Redemption 2, and more in the coming months,” Microsoft added in today’s announcement.

I have no idea how many Xbox Ones are still out in the wild, or how many people may be tempted to blow the dust off of them instead of upgrading to a current-gen console. But given the ongoing price hikes for both the PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, it’s a really nice option for those who can’t otherwise afford to buy new hardware this fall for GTA 6.

Reflector Entertainment had a new game in pre-production, but Bandai decided it wasn't worth the time or money to pursue.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Two years after the release of Unknown 9: Awakening, its one and only game, Bandai Namco's Reflector Entertainment is closing.

The shutdown was revealed in a notice posted by Banda Namco (via Game Informer) saying the company "has passed a resolution to dissolve and liquidate its consolidated subsidiary Reflector Entertainment." The decision was made "after comprehensively considering future business plans, necessary additional investment, and the possibility of profitability and business continuation," Bandai Namco said.

Unknown 9: Awakening, featuring The Witcher star Anya Chalotra as a woman able to travel into a mysterious dimension known as the Fold, showed potential in our pre-release preview as a "linear, narrative-driven, set-piece laden" game drawing from Xbox 360 releases of the late 2000s.

The full game, however, landed with a thud. A month after launch, Reflector laid off 18% of its workforce; a few months after that, in January 2025, more layoffs followed as an in-development project was cancelled. Reflector CEO Herve Hoerdt said at the time that the decision "correlates directly with the failure of the studio's ambitious and courageous first project [Unknown 9: Awakening]," which "didn't come near the company expectations."

Reflector confirmed the coming end of operations in its own message on LinkedIn, writing that "after reviewing the progress of our latest project in pre-production, future development requirements, and current market conditions, Bandai Namco concluded that it could not justify several more years of investment."

Bandai Namco said the liquidation of Reflector Entertainment is expected to happen "once the necessary procedures according to local laws are completed," but a concrete schedule has not been set.

#3691. Mortal Kombat 2 Is Winning The Race To Become Mortal Kombat 2

What's in a name? That's the question that Mortal Kombat studio CCO Ed Boon is asking, as he recently set up a few polls asking for opinions on what the next Mortal Kombat game should be called. According to Boon, three possible names were on the table: Mortal Kombat 12, Mortal Kombat 13, or Mortal Kombat 2.

"Footnote: Some people are assuming the title with the most votes will determine where we take the story," Boon wrote online. "That’s not the case. We’ve just had difficulty kounting lately."

The current naming convention for Mortal Kombat doesn't make much sense if you've taken a break from the franchise. The series made a successful comeback in 2011 with Mortal Kombat, the ninth installment in the franchise. This was followed by Mortal Kombat X in 2015 and Mortal Kombat 11 in 2019, which brought the original storyline that began in 1992's Mortal Kombat to a close. This was followed by a soft reboot in 2023 with Mortal Kombat 1, which remixed established story beats and put familiar characters in new roles.

To make things even more confusing, Mortal Kombat 1 heavily references multiple timelines toward the end of its campaign, drawing in characters from across a Mortal Kombat multiverse for a final showdown against Shang Tsung from the previous timeline. The Khaos Reigns expansion would also touch on these ideas, as the Titan version of Havik sought to merge all timelines into one.

Currently, "Mortal Kombat 2" is leading the votes with 45.2% of people polled by Boon favoring that title, at the time of writing. If this becomes the title of the next Mortal Kombat game, it will be the second Mortal Kombat 2, which will probably confuse anyone who hasn't been following along. While it hasn't been officially revealed yet, Boon did confirm that Mortal Kombat developer NetherRealm Studios is "pursuing another Mortal Kombat game," and he added that "other forms of media and whatnot" for the Mortal Kombat franchise are in development.

That was back in May, and since then, Mortal Kombat's parent company, Warner Bros. Interactive, has seen some big changes. Paramount’s $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery eventually went through, leading to the merger between Warner Bros. Interactive and Paramount Games Studio. That new entity puts Mortal Kombat, Game of Thrones, Batman, and a treasure trove of IP under the same roof as Avatar: The Last Airbender, South Park, and Star Trek. Tony Driscoll, president of games and experiences at Skydance, will oversee the new division.

Robert Downey Jr. has a habit of stealing the spotlight, and apparently, he has also stolen a Marvel Cinematic Universe record from one of his oldest co-stars. With Avengers: Doomsday hitting the 2026 movie calendar and bringing the former Iron Man actor back as Doctor Doom, Paul Bettany has lost something he briefly had all to himself. Judging by his reaction, he's taking it about as well as you'd expect from the man who used to live inside Tony Stark's computers.

Bettany, who is back playing Vision in the series VisionQuest, streaming with a Disney+ subscription, was recently asked about Downey's return during an interview with BBC Radio 1's Ali Plumb, who posted a clip of his interview to his Instagram. The actor pointed out that after Downey's exit in Avengers: Endgame, he could claim to be the MCU's longest-serving performer. Then Marvel decided to bring back his old boss. As Bettany joked in the video below, he said his former Avengers pal was stealing his “legacy.”

I love that he's treating this like yet another indignity Tony Stark has inflicted on him. Honestly, if you've spent nearly two decades working within the MCU, you deserve at least a little time to enjoy being the franchise's longest-serving employee. Unfortunately, Downey has apparently returned to collect his old parking space, too. As he hilariously put it:

He stole my legacy, as he has stolen so many other things from me. Maybe I still outlast him. We'll see.

The funny thing is that Bettany was there from the beginning. When 2008's Iron Man kicked off the MCU, the British actor voiced J.A.R.V.I.S., the artificially intelligent assistant helping Tony build suits, monitor threats and occasionally deliver a perfectly timed sarcastic comment. He didn't even have to show his face to become one of the franchise's most familiar performers.

Then, in 2015, Avengers: Age of Ultron gave him an actual body as Vision. Since then, Bettany has played the synthezoid across several Marvel movies as well as the TV show WandaVision and its aforementioned spinoff series, VisionQuest. That's an impressive career for someone who originally signed up to record a disembodied computer voice.

Downey, of course, was also there in 2008. He headlined Iron Man and helped turn Marvel into a box-office juggernaut before Tony's death in 2019's Endgame. Bettany kept appearing in new MCU projects after that, which gave him a brief moment atop the seniority chart. But with Downey officially playing Victor von Doom in December's Doomsday, the two actors will once again share a franchise history stretching back to the same first movie. So I wouldn't exactly call this a formal record being smashed. It's Bettany's wonderfully petty description of losing an exclusive bragging right.

And I hope their friendly rivalry continues. Bettany has previously spoken about how meaningful Vision has become to fans, especially those who identify with the character's struggle to belong. The actor's own MCU future remains open after VisionQuest, and he hasn't been officially confirmed for Doomsday. So, for the moment, his next opportunity to outlast Downey is still anybody's guess.

As for Downey, I'm curious to see how Marvel handles the actor who helped establish its cinematic universe now playing one of its most dangerous villains. Doomsday arrives on December 18 as part of the slate of upcoming new superhero movies, with Avengers: Secret Wars scheduled for the 2027 release calendar.

I'm rooting for Bettany to reclaim his title eventually, if only because I want to hear how he delivers the news. After all these years as J.A.R.V.I.S. and Vision, surely the man deserves to win one argument with Tony Stark.

#3689. David Faustino Sends Support to Christina Applegate After Misdiagnosis

David Faustino is sharing his support for former Married … With Children costar Christina Applegate after she revealed she was misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis.

“You know, I see her on a regular basis,” Faustino, 52, told Us exclusively while attending Cure Addiction Now‘s 3rd annual fundraising evening at The Beverly Hills Hotel on Monday, November 9. “We hang out, and I just am there supporting her through this journey and discovery of what’s really going on, and just loving her and knowing that the best will happen for her.”

Faustino and Applegate, 54, played siblings on the beloved Fox sitcom, which aired from 1987 to 1997. The actor has often praised Applegate for how she’s navigated her health battle in the public eye.

Applegate initially announced in 2021 that she was diagnosed with MS. She was vocal about her symptoms and experience in the years that followed, but she revealed in October that she was misdiagnosed.

“[My doctor] came into my room and said, ‘Congratulations, you don’t have MS,'” she said on her “MeSsY” podcast. “I was, like, not happy at all. Everybody else was so happy.”

Applegate admitted that she was struggling with the news. “You don’t get misdiagnosed and then all of the sudden I’m better. … If anything, I’ve gotten worse,” she continued. “So I’m back at square one where I don’t know what’s going on with me. And that’s going to be an online investigation that my doctors are going to be getting into just to find out what has been going on since 2021, why did this happen?”

In a separate episode, Applegate vowed to stay involved in the MS community despite her changing diagnosis. She further revealed that she’s taken steps to explore other possible avenues, including lupus, Lyme disease and rheumatoid arthritis.

“I’m being tested for those things slowly but surely,” she said. “I lived as a person with MS for almost six years.”

Earlier this year, Faustino opened up to Us about watching his friend work through her health challenges.

“I admire her being strong in the face of this, even though it’s been a real blow. It’s been very hard for her, but she does keep her humor,” he told Us in June, adding that Applegate has maintained her “dry, sarcastic sense of humor since the moment I met her.”

Faustino is now going down memory lane with his own podcast, “The Bundy Club,” where he gets to revisit the series that introduced him to Applegate.

“We just started it a few months ago, but we take episodes and we break those episodes down, and we have a guest. So I’m having to rewatch the show, and quite honestly, it’s funny,” he told Us on Monday. “It makes me laugh, and I can see why people still like it. And nowadays, it’s comfort television, you know?”

And while his kids got in on the fun for Halloween in Married … With Children costumes, Faustino joked they couldn’t “care less” about watching their dad’s show.

“It was my wife Lindsay’s idea,” he said of the group costume. “She tried to get me to do it last year. I was like, ‘Nah.’ This year, I gave in. We had zero idea that it was gonna go viral like that. … People just loved it.”

#3688. GTA 6 Preloading Is Officially Live, Files Mention Multiplayer And PS5 Pro Features

At long last, you can now install Grand Theft Auto 6 on your console via preloading, or at least you can if you live in Australia or New Zealand. Preloading begins in all regions at midnight local time, so people in the US are almost there.

With preloading now live, people have dug through the files and found things they weren't intended to see. That includes references to things like "join Session," "launch Activity," and "launch Multiplayer Activity." People are taking these to be references to a new form of GTA Online.

Rockstar has said GTA 6 is a single-player game, but it’s expected to add some form of online multiplayer at some point. Just because "Multiplayer" was found in the game's files, that doesn't necessarily mean online functionality will be available at launch--it's likely coming sometime later.

People have theorized that GTA 6's story and Online could be separate games. That remains to be seen, but those who have the game preloaded have discovered that GTA 6's "Story" is an individual download within the game's files. Whatever the case, experts and insiders believe GTA 6's new online experience will launch at some point in 2027.

Additionally, the datamining effort led to some discoveries about what Rockstar might be cooking up in terms of PS5 Pro support. People believe they found references to 120Hz support on PS5 Pro, along with multi-frame super resolution, which is known as PSSR on PS5 Pro.

Rockstar has yet to announce any specifics about GTA 6 for PS5 Pro, and the game's trailers so far have been captured on a standard PS5.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. For more, check out the exact worldwide launch times. The game's non-simultaneous launch means people in the US will be among the last in the world to get in. Bungie has served up our first proper look at Marathon's big Symbiosis update, which is set to go live on December 8 with a permanent PvE mode, plus an all-new Team Deathmatch mode and a social space called Limbo.

Symbiosis represents the start of "the evolution of Marathon," Bungie said, with "a plethora of updates and changes" to the game. First and foremost is the addition of Marathon's PvE mode, now permanent and with a new name, Expedition, that's described in the teaser as a "co-op PvE roguelite." Details beyond that haven't been revealed just yet, but Bungie called it "phase one" of the team's PvE plan, suggesting that it remains a work in progress.

Also notable in Symbiosis is the addition of Limbo, a "social space" where players can hang out without getting aired out (although there does appear to be a little area set aside for friendly shootin'), and its firing range, a handy way to test the game's guns without having to venture into its less friendly locales.

Speaking of which, the Perimeter map is being expanded with new points of interest and tunnels, and a new sword-wielding runner shell, Bishop, will debut with the update. For those who prefer the PvP life, the update will also kick off a beta for Marathon's Team Deathmatch mode.

Overall, Symbiosis looks to be a pretty big deal, and while today's tease is light on detail, the early reaction among players on Reddit and social media seems quite positive. Bishop is already racking up fans:

One other bit of good news: The rollout of Symbiosis on December 8 will also mark the start of an "open play week," during which the game will be fully free to play, including the new modes and content. If you dig it and decide to stick around (ie., buy the game), any progress and items earned will carry over.

#3686. Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Water Temple Walkthrough

Nintendo Switch 2The Legend of ZeldaThe Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time

Well, you’ve made it. You’re finally at the most infamous dungeon in all of Zelda-dom, the Water Temple of Ocarina of Time. Good news for you: In the remake, this dungeon is far, far easier than it’s ever been. A few of the edges have been sanded down, the rooms all look far more distinct and memorable so it’s less of a mental maze, and the iron boots can be equipped and de-equipped simply by pressing down on the gamepad. Compared to the original, it’s a smooth ride. But still, this is one of the most involved dungeons in the game, so buckle on that Zora Tunic and let’s get swimming.

To enter the Water Temple, you need to be wearing (no, I wasn’t joking) the Zora Tunic, which you get by freeing King Zora from his ice block back in Zora Domain. To do that, you need Blue Fire in a bottle, which you obtain in the Ice Cavern as an adult. You’ll also need the Iron Boots from that same cavern. If you haven’t gotten that far yet, back yourself up and come back to this guide later.

Once you’re in the temple, remove your iron boots and float to the top. Run forward, and you’ll be in a big, open room with a bunch of doors on all four sides across four different floors, and water below you. I’m going to be referring to this as the “main hall” going forward. We’re going to be here a lot. I’ll also be referring to doors by floor and cardinal direction, so if you’re ever confused about what I’m talking about, open that map.

The first thing you’re going to do is slay that Blue Tektite in front of you. Sword, hookshot, whatever you like, just get it out of the way.

Next, you’re going to equip those Iron Boots, descend to the first floor, and head through the east door. Once you’re inside, remove the boots to float upward for a cutscene with your fiancee, Ruto. When it’s over, grab the Dungeon Map from the chest in front of you, and then stand on the platform with the Triforce symbol and play Zelda’s Lullaby to lower the water level.

Real quick tip: There are three different spots to mess with the water level in this dungeon, and each one will raise it to a different spot. This one brings it down to the first floor, and is marked by glowy blue pillars. It might be good to make a note somewhere of which color results in which water level, just in case you ever get turned around or confused and the water level is in the wrong place.

Once the water has dropped, fearlessly jump down the hole, landing in the water below so it doesn’t damage you. Now, with the water taken care of, note that one of the torches in here is lit. Stand behind it with your bow equipped and aim an arrow through the fire to each of the two torches on the other end of the room to open the door in front of you, then enter. Defeat the three Spikes by blocking their attacks with your shield and swinging your sword when they’re vulnerable to obtain a Small Key. (Din’s Fire is also usable for this puzzle).

Backtrack the way you came in and head out into the main hall. There are two more aptly named Spikes out here waiting for you; get rid of them. To your left (west side, 1F) is a bombable/breakable wall. Knock that out, and use your Iron Boots to sink, sink, sink. Head down the underwater corridor and take care of the Shell Blade by hitting it with your hookshot when its mouth is all the way open. At the end of the corridor, take off the boots and rise up.

In here, climb the platform jutting out of the water and use the hookshot to grapple onto the pillars ahead of you. Take down the Tektites and the Like Like (Hookshot is great here), and you’ll be rewarded with the Compass. Now, all the way back to the main hall!

To the west (1F) is a block you can push forward until it drops in the water. Do that, then use the boots to sink again. Look out for the Shell Blade in the way, then rise back up at the end of the hall. You’ll find yourself in a room with a whirlpool and some statues underwater, and a chest on the other side.

This looks trickier than it is. Use the iron boots to drop into the whirlpool, aiming for the center platform (the serpent’s body) stretched down the middle of the pool. Stand on the platform and use your hookshot to smack the weird gem thing in the serpent’s mouth. This will unlock the underwater grate, allowing you to enter. You might need to don and doff the iron boots a few times to swim over properly, but with some careful aiming it’s very doable. There are two more Shell Blades to fight inside, after which you’re free to take off the boots, rise to the surface, and grab the small key.

Back across the whirlpool, out the door, into the main hall again. There’s a locked door on the central pillar here, directly in front of you, and you now have a key. Head inside.

Once inside, step forward, turn around, and look up for a grapple point. Use your hookshot to get on the platform above. Right in front of you is a spot to stand and play Zelda’s Lullaby to raise the water back up. (Note: the columns here are green, green brings the water to 2F! Write it down if you need to!) Before you leave this inside pillar, though, jump in the water and look down: a new gap has opened up with the water level rising.

Use iron boots to drop down, where three Spikes are waiting for you. Kill them with the hookshot, then use the hookshot to hit the green switch above your head, releasing a Shell Blade. Kill that too, then remove the iron boots where it was standing to rise up into the now-open area. There’s a red rupee in a chest on the way up, as well as a gold skulltula on the wall opposite. Funny, I feel like something else used to be here in the original game…anyway, grab these, backtrack the way you came in, and take off the boots to rise back up into the middle of the pillar. Then swim out the door into the main hall.

Directly in front of you across the water (2F, east side) is a bombable/hammerable wall in an alcove. You know what to do. Smash the pots for bombs if needed, otherwise use the Megaton Hammer if you’ve cleared the Fire Temple already, and head on through.

Be cautious as you head into the water and equip the Iron Boots. There are four Stingers waiting for you. Your hookshot will take care of them, but it’s easy to get overwhelmed, so take it slow (not that you can do otherwise with those boots on). Once they’re dead, proceed to the end of the underwater hallway and unequip the boots to rise to the surface.

In front of you is a pool of water with a switch in it, and a round platform being lifted by a fountain. Use your hookshot to hit the switch to lower the platform, stand on the platform, then use hookshot again on the same switch to raise yourself up to the floor above. Your reward is a Small Key. Take it, then backtrack all the way to the main hall again.

In the main hall, hop in the water and swim around the central pillar to the locked door directly across from where you just entered. It’s got glowing red columns around itâcan’t miss it. Use the Small Key and head inside. Smack the switch and ready yourself; a blue Tektite will descend and try to fight you. Once it’s dispatched, stand on the lowered platform and use your hookshot to hit the switch again and rise up.

It’s another Zelda’s Lullaby spot, this time with red lights, that will bring the water to 3F! Play that same song! Up goes the water. Jump down from the ledge next to the Triforce symbol and back into the water of the main room.

Mind any Tektites you haven’t dispatched already and swim on over to 3F, west side, for another locked door for which you conveniently have a key.

A couple of Keese will be waiting for you to slash them up. Take stock of your surroundings before you proceed. You’ll want to use the hookshot to grapple your way up these moving platforms to the top, one by one. Start by dropping down to the platform below the one you start on, and it’ll descend until you can grapple across. Then just work your way up, one by one. Don’t panic, it’s very doable, and there’s a stable platform to the side you can jump to if you need a second to collect yourself. Head through the door at the top once you reach it.

In this next room, I started by hitting all the Tektites below with my arrows just to get them out of the way. Then, use your hookshot to hit the switch at the center of the room and make the grapple points raise up. You’ll want to grapple to the first point directly in front of you, then (counterintuitively) hit the switch again to lower the points. Use the grapple point on the next wall to crossâyou’ll be able to continue along the ledge only if the grapple point pillars are lowered. Hit the switch yet again and grapple to the final pillar, hit the switchÂ again to lower the pillars. Climb atop the one next to you, then hit the switch one final time to raise the pillar and lift you within reach of the next floor.

Hit those pots for health, arrows, whatever before you go through the door, it’s time for one of the best bosses in the game!

Shadow Link is tough; he mirrors your moves! Don’t attack him head-on while his shield is up or he’ll do something I hear the kids call “aura farming.” I was able to beat him pretty easily by keeping my guard up and dodging his combos, waiting for an opening. In the first phase of the fight, I would dodge to the left side twice whenever he swung, then would come in for a combo toward his exposed back. In the second phase, this was trickier, but still very doable if I dodged backwards twice and then threw out the hookshot to stun him. Make sure you dodge backwards far enough when he gears up for a spin attack, and don’t let yourself get pushed too close to the arena walls, or he can pin you down for some big damage.

With Shadow Link down, head through the door opposite where you came in (use your map if you got turned around) to finally obtain the Longshot, which will let you hookshot targets even farther away than before! To escape this room, aim for the very far away targets above you, then drop down the waterfall into the cavern below. Let yourself float down the river, but mind the whirlpoolsâyou can use the iron boots to just walk between them underwater. About three-quarters of the way down the river, there’s a gold skulltula on a wall above you. Make sure you’re firmly iron-booted underwater, then use the longshot to smack it once to defeat it, and then again to collect the token.

Climb atop the stone outcropping on the end of the river and use the longshot again, once to hit the eye above the gates and open them, and again to grapple to the grapple point on the other side of the gates before they close on you.

We’re back in familiar territory, so head out to the main hall once again. We’ve still got some work to do, and we’re sorely in want of a boss key right about now. First, we need to get the water level down. Get those boots on and drop down to 1F east, the room where you first ran into Ruto. Swim up to the Triforce and play Zelda’s Lullaby to drop the water, then head back into the main hall. Then, you want to enter the central pillar again from the door on 1F. We’re here to raise the water level, but hold up. Grapple to the Triforce stand, then look at the ceiling for a grapple point you can now reach with the longshot. Fly on up there, then look across to the other side of the ceiling for another gold skulltula. Once you have that, drop back down and play Zelda’s Lullaby.

Everything’s in place! Exit the pillar and run around the central platform to stand on the floating block, looking across at the outer wall. You should see a gate with a grapple point on the other side, and an eye switch above. Once again, use the longshot to hit the eye, then immediately use it again on the grapple to get through. Drop into the pool and equip the iron boots, then walk into the hallway. There’s a movable block wedged into the wall hereâpull it out as far as you can, blocking off the hallway, then take off the boots and swim up and out of the pool. You should be able to see a fence ahead of you with a waterfall on the other side, and a grapple point on the ceiling. Grapple to it with the longshot, use the iron boots to sink into the water, then head down the hallway and push the block out of your way to clear a path to the chest with yet another small key.

Back to the main hall again, equipping the iron boots again and sinking down to 1F, north. Grapple across the gap and use your small key on the door. Inside, there are a lot of tektites in the way. Use your sword, shield, bow, whatever, to get them out of the way (seriously, they will knock you into whirlpools otherwise). Carefully cross the room, avoiding the boulders, using the iron boots as needed to stay out of whirlpools, and go through the door. In here, use the longshot to dispatch all the stingers, then smash the rock walls (with bombs or the megaton hammer) to reveal a block that can be pushed into the water to hit a switch. The switch will raise the water level for you to head out the door in the wall above.

Whew. Almost done. In here, step on the switch to raise platforms you can jump across, and a tektite with them. Get rid of it (and the other tektite on the other side of the room) as you see fit, then cross and go through the opening. On the other side, be careful. Boulders are rolling down this stream and will run you over if you step in at the wrong time. Wait for one to pass, then go under the waterfall and immediately turn to the left to jump into the alcove. There’s a shell blade waiting, so get that out of the way. Before you head through the door, turn back, wait for the boulder to pass, then jump back in the stream, through the waterfall, and look upâthere’s another gold skulltula near the ceiling. Grab it fast, then turn back and head through the door to, at long last, claim the boss key.

Great work, folks! Turn back, follow the boulders down the stream and into the room you were in earlier with the boulders and whirlpools, then back into the main hall. I’m sorry to say we’ve got to mess with the water levels one more time. You’ll need to go back into 2F west, head up the fountain, and play Zelda’s Lullaby one last time to raise the water and open a path up the big stairs to the north on 2F (technically 3F). Drop down, and head that direction. You’ll have to stand on the platform of the central pillar and longshot your way over. Load up on hearts from the pots before you go in, and get ready to fight.

Okay, not yet. Use your iron boots in this room to climb the waterfall and avoid the spiky things spinning back and forth.Â Now get ready to fight!

Morpha isn’t too bad, as bosses go. The boss itself is the weird red Metroid-looking ball thingie that’s hiding in the tentacles. Your main goal is to use the longshot to rip it out of its watery protection and whack it a bunch with your sword. This is pretty easy with Navi’s targeting; the main thing you need to worry about is getting hit by water tentacles. Morpha will manifest these out of the water and try and slam them on the ground near you. Early on, they’ll be pretty spread out, but later in the fight they’ll form a big wall that’s harder to avoid. If you get trapped you can also use the grapple points on the sides of the room to fly out of danger. I tried to stay on the edges as much as possible; you never really want to be in the water with Morpha. But you can use the central platforms to bait Morpha into an easier spot for you to longshot the ball out, or just to cross out of the way of attacks. Try to be aware of where Morpha the Ball is at all times, as this fight can get annoying if it’s always all the way across the room, just out of range. Use those grapple points!

That’s the Water Temple done, folks! Enjoy the cutscenes, and get the heck outta there to see how the Zora are doing.

Oh, psst. Once the cutscenes are over, you’ll be at Lake Hylia, just before sunrise. Check out the stone monument in front of you to make good use of that timing. You’re welcome!

#3685. Former PlayStation Boss Thinks Sony Is Solving The Wrong Problem With PS6

Sony confirmed last week that development on its "next-generation" PlayStation platform will pick up speed in 2027, but not everyone is convinced the world needs a PS6 right now. In an interview with The Trophy Room, former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden said true innovation would come from finding a way to lower the price of the PS5, allowing more potential buyers to enter the market.

"I think we have enough power in the machine. The innovation needs to come not from making PS6 for $1,200, it's to make another PS5 for $300. Now, that would be true innovation," Layden said, while also remarking how the PS5 generation saw price increases over time, not reductions.

Compared to previous generations, the PS5 has only gotten more expensive in the six years that it has been on the market, rising from $400 to $600 for the PS5 Digital Edition, while the PS5 with a disc drive has increased from $500 to $650. The PS5 Pro has seen the biggest increase in the few years it has been around, as the beefier machine has jumped from its original price of $700 to $900. Various factors are to blame, but one of the biggest is the global memory shortage that has hit all fields of technology, thanks to AI data centers eating into the world's supply.

A PS6 that costs over $1,000 will be out of reach for many consumers, and as Layden believes, it likely won't be as big a graphical leap forward as we've seen in previous PlayStation generations. While the difference in video game graphics between the PS1 and the PS2 was especially noticeable, later consoles have shown diminishing returns, and Layden believes the graphical quality of PS6 games will be even harder to notice. "These are the differences that only dogs can hear," Layden said about the reported increase in teraflops and ray-tracing power the PS6 will supposedly offer.

"What the company needs to do is do what it's never done, which is don't iterate the console. Make it smaller, make it cheaper, do all the things you can around that. The silicon is fine, the operating system is fine. It's more than enough power to build the kind of games all of us want to play."

As the current generation continues, Sony has also sought to extend the PS5's lifespan with new ideas, like a PS5 Pro-inspired upscaling tech called Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR). While it's only available for two games currently, QSSR could give the PS5 plenty of staying power in the current gaming generation and the next.

As of late, 90 Day Fiancé's Sarper Güven has been dipping his toes into the world of stand-up comedy. That venture is apparently proving to be fruitful as well, as he's allegedly making bank, if these latest court filings are to be believed. As Sarper and Shekinah continue to navigate the divorce process following their time on The Last Resort, it's being alleged that he has cleared over six figures from touring over the past year.

The latest news comes from TMZ, which reports that Shekinah is seeking thousands in monthly spousal support. It's a steep sum, even with both coming off the 2026 TV schedule where they netted pay for appearances within the TLC franchise. If these numbers are accurate, however, I'm shocked to say it might be justified.

Per a post on TMZ's Threads account, Shekinah wants $6,189 a month in spousal support, as well as reimbursement for $35,000 in legal fees. She went on to claim in court documents that Sarper's stand-up comedy netted $280,000 on their joint tax returns, with a $180,000 net profit.

I find that number more jaw-dropping than Sarper's body count. Sure, I'd previously written about him selling out comedy shows, but 90 Day Fiancé fans have witnessed a lot of his comedy already. I personally hadn't seen anything on TV that convinced me his stand-up was worth the price of admission, but it would seem some people do!

Shekinah also alleged in the court documents that her own business suffered a net loss of $55,000 due to her closing down the business temporarily to support Sarper on tour. The only thing I can think of is how ironic it is that Sarper might not be on the line for any of this had he signed the prenuptial agreement like she originally requested.

While none have ever presented a full pay stub to see, the general consensus amongst 90 Day stars is that they don't make a ton of money doing the show. To that point, Stephanie Matto alleged she only made a couple thousand dollars per episode. Also, while it's true that not all cast members are paid the same, many of them keep their day jobs in addition to doing the show.

90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way Just Hit On Andi And Nigel's Biggest Issue, And I Don't See Them Getting Over It

All this to say, while some reality shows allow their stars enough money that they can live off that alone, that doesn't seem to be the case for 90 Day stars. That makes it even wilder that Sarper has reportedly made so much money from his stand-up comedy work alone, especially when he's playing relatively small venues.

As these divorce proceedings continue, it'll be interesting to see what information may come out as a result. Shekinah and Sarper were on 90 Day Fiancé for many seasons, and I'd be curious to see what, if anything, comes out about the show as they make filings.

Neither of the two is currently on 90 Day Fiancé, but Sarper is rumored to be returning in a future season of The Single Life. As for Shekinah, she's allegedly done appearing on TLC, but we'll see if she follows through on that promise.

#3683. 'Cold Blooded: Who Killed These Girls?' Depicts 1991 Yogurt Shop Murders

ABC News Podcast Network and 20/20 are shedding light on true crime stories with two new podcasts, including “Cold Blooded: Who Killed These Girls?” which will take a deep dive into the infamous 1991 quadruple murder at a yogurt shop in Austin, Texas, that launched a 34-year investigation.

In the trailer exclusively obtained by Us, 20/20 editorial producer Cristina Corbin explains that solving the case “would take decades” after teens Amy Ayers, Jennifer Harbison, Sarah Harbison and Eliza Thomas were murdered at I Can’t Believe It’s Yogurt! in December 1991. The girls were found gagged, tied up and shot in the head inside of the yogurt shop, and the building was later set on fire in an attempt to hide evidence of the crime.

“As a journalist, I’ve been following this story for years. I’ve traveled to Austin and I’ve spent time with both the investigators and the families of the victims,” Corbin says in the trailer. “Certain details of this case haunt me. Certain questions linger. In this series, I want to answer some of those questions about that night in the yogurt shop and everything that happened after.”

The case went unsolved for decades until the Austin Police Department announced in September 2025 that advanced Y-STR DNA profiles and autosomal DNA was able to match serial killer and rapist Robert Eugene Brashers to the crime. Brashers died by suicide in 1999 when he got into a standoff with police.

Brashers had a lengthy criminal history, and it’s suspected that he committed at least three murders between 1990 and 1998 across South Carolina and Missouri.

The network also gave Us exclusive details about another upcoming podcast titled “Britain’s Most Notorious Crimes.”

“Britain’s Most Notorious Crimes” (working title) will take a look at some of the U.K.’s most high-profile crime cases over the years, including the crimes of Ben Needham, Joanna Yeates, Jane Andrews and Peter Tobin. The podcast will include interviews and fresh revelations that share a deeper look into the disturbing true crime stories.

Capcom still hasn't announced a release date for Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance, the Sunbreak-scale DLC that was revealed in February, but it seems like we might be getting a chance to sample the expansion before too long. A recent Steam listing update has provided a strong reason to suspect that there'll be a public beta for Ascendance available ahead of its launch in 2027.

As SteamDB changelogs show, the Steam app entry for Monster Hunter Wilds' 2024 public beta was quietly updated early this morning to change the app's name from "Monster Hunter Wilds Beta test" to "Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance Beta test." Similarly, the listing's visual assets were updated to feature key art of a hunter facing an Arateka, one of the new monsters being introduced in the expansion.

And sure enough, while the Wilds beta was removed from player libraries after it ended, it's possible for users who'd previously played it to confirm its listing changes within the Steam app by viewing their own played games from their Steam profile. I just looked. It says Ascendance right there.

As the previous Wilds beta consisted of a repackaged demo build, it's likely that an Ascendance beta would follow suit: I'd expect a similar set of hunts to what in-person attendees were able to get hands-on time with at Tokyo Game Show in September, offering a chance to try out the new Boost Bracer weapon mechanics in Master Rank combat.

If a beta does materialize, it'll hopefully be a smoother experience than what beta hunters got in 2024. The early Wilds playtest was the first time PC players encountered the dreaded origami monsters, a symptom of the severe optimization issues that tanked Wilds' reputation for over a year after launch.

As for when that beta might be available, we can only speculate—but given that Monster Hunter has made prior appearances at Geoff Keighley productions, a public playtest that accompanies a hypothetical Game Awards trailer makes intuitive sense. But I'm just reading the tea leaves here—Capcom hasn't said a word about when it'll offer its next DLC teaser.

Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance is set to launch some time in 2027.

#3679. Student Game Development Competition Shut Down Because Kids Kept Submitting AI Slop

This will be the last year for the Australian STEM Videogame Challenge, a competition for young people, as the entries have grown overrun with AI-generated slop. According to a report in PC Gamer the event, which has been around for 12 years, will cease operations because it was getting too difficult to determine which games were made with AI and which were made entirely by the kids themselves.

The contest was open to students from elementary to high school, and required kids either working alone or in groups of up to four people to submit a game based on a chosen theme complete with a design document and a short trailer showing off the game. On Reddit, a parent of a child who regularly submitted games to the competition lamented the competition’s shutdown. “My teenage son and his friends entered the competition for several years, meeting up regularly, discussing ideas, and working together on a shared passion project,” the parent wrote. “It gave them something exciting to work on, and a common goal to strive towards outside of school. It also gave them confidence, and made them feel part of a wider community.”

In a statement to PC Gamer, Cathy Zemaitis, head of the Student Learning and Progress division at ACER, the company that puts on the challenge, said, “The decision was driven by the rapid and complex rise of generative AI in game development, making it harder to judge what students made themselves, and moving the program away from its original purpose.”

The “justification” for using AI in a professional game development setting is to essentially make games faster and more cheaply. One of the stated purposes of the challenge is to “enable students to develop real-world skills.” How is that accomplished using AI tools, especially at an age when core game development skills haven’t yet been learned? I’d imagine not very effectively. And it really sucks that the example adults are setting with the push for and normalization of generative AI is resulting in the end of a valuable opportunity for the next generation to develop a skill. We are eating the game development seed corn.

“I know as adults the world can be unfair, and we need to adapt,” the parent on Reddit wrote. “But this really hit home for me, because the victims this time are children. My son was visibly gutted when I told him the news, and it genuinely felt like part of his identity had been destroyed.”

The actor is starting to book gigs again.

Johnny Depp was wrapped up in legal issues and personal matters during the early 2020s, with the biggest situation being his defamation case with former wife Amber Heard. The Oscar nominee received a mostly favorable verdict in 2022 and, since then, he’s been easing his way back into the entertainment industry. On that note, his latest feature is the 2026 movie schedule entry, Ebenezer. Now, amid this phase of his career, one of Depp’s most recent producers is getting real about the prospect of his comeback.

In 2023, Depp starred in the French historical drama film Jeanne du Barry, and the film sees him play the role of Louis XV. Nellee Holmes served as one of the executive producers on that film, and she recently spoke to CNN as part of a wide ranging story on Depp. Holmes was quite complimentary of the actor, calling him a “good human being.” In the producer’s estimation, Depp has forged connections with “people who trust him” and still believe in him. As for the quality of the leading man’s work, Holmes had this to say:

You cannot say anything that makes him bad. His work is his weapon.

In terms of Jeanne du Barry, the film generated headlines several years back due to being Depp’s first post-trial movie. The biopic was directed by Maïwenn, who also co-starred alongside Depp as the titular character. Ultimately, the movie debuted at the Cannes Film Festival in May 2023, and Depp received a standing ovation. Despite that praise, Maïwenn would later claim Depp was “difficult” to work with due to creative differences and personal conduct.

All that aside, though, Holmes is of the belief that Ebenezer will mark a turning point for Depp. The film was announced back in October 2025 and, at that time, it was also confirmed that horror maven Ti West would direct it. Months ago, West praised Depp’s portrayal of the titular Ebenezer Scrooge, noting that he possesses that “cadence and that musicality to the way that he performs.”. Another bit of praise came from Depp’s co-star, Rupert Grint, who simply referred to him as “so iconic.”

This holiday flick isn’t the only production Depp has on the horizon either. He’s also set to headline Day Drinker, which is a supernatural thriller film from director Marc Webb that’s set to be released amid the 2027 movie schedule. There have also been rumblings regarding a third Pirates of the Caribbean film being in the works, thanks to comments from producer Jerry Bruckheimer. It’s unknown if Depp would star in the film, but he joked about possibly not being able to grow facial hair again should he reprise Captain Jack Sparrow.

Ironically, amid talk about Depp making a “comeback” in Hollywood, he prefers not to use that term. Depp previously admitted to being confused by the word being applied to his circumstances, because he “didn’t go anywhere” to begin with. Still, it does indeed seem that the star’s career is on an upward trajectory and, all the while, he seems to have people like Nelle Holmes and Ti West in his corner.

Check out Johnny Depp in Ebenezer when it opens in theaters on November 13. Also, be on the lookout for Day Drinker, which is set to hit cinemas on March 26, 2027.

#3677. Celebrity Accused of Misconduct Is Named After Attempt to Hide Identity

British comedian David Walliams has been accused of sexual misconduct after previously attempting to conceal his identity.

Walliams, a children’s book author and judge on Britain’s Got Talent, was officially named in a report by The Guardian on Tuesday, November 10. According to the outlet, multiple women accused Walliams, now 55, of using his status to groom them. Two of the accusers, who are now in their 30s, were allegedly 15 when they met Walliams.

The allegations reportedly span decades. Walliams was identified following a lengthy investigation by The Guardian and ITV News.

Walliams previously sought an injunction against the media companies in order to prevent his name from being released, with his lawyers claiming he was a suicide risk. The request was denied by a judge earlier this month.

Last year, Walliams’ entire back catalog of published works was dropped by HarperCollins following an internal investigation over “inappropriate behavior” toward female employees. The Guardian alleged Walliams had a sexual relationship with a junior member of staff at the publishing company.

Walliams denied the accusations against him in a statement published Tuesday.

“Looking back, I realize that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with,” he began. “I realize I did not always take people’s feelings properly into account. That is something I regret. And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something I never did.”

Walliams insisted, “I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me.”

During court proceedings earlier this month, Walliams’ attorney, Sara Mansoori KC, noted he had “been hospitalized for months” and “has no intention of returning to public life” amid the ongoing scandal.

The attorney representing the media organizations involved in the case, meanwhile, argued Walliams’ alleged victims were also “traumatized” by his behavior and “have suffered mental health crises” of their own. The lawyer further argued “the obligation falls on the hospital” to keep Walliams safe and his mental health is not the responsibility of the media outlets.

If you have experienced sexual assault, call the National Sexual Assault Telephone Hotline at 1-800-656-4673 for confidential support.

If you or someone you know is struggling or in crisis, help is available. Call or text 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org.

A South Carolina man has been arrested after allegedly leaving his six-year-old daughter in line at Target at 1 AM to save his spot for Pokemon trading cards.

#3674. Sadie Robertson Says Marriage 'Shifted' After Mom Noticed Their Struggles

Sadie Robertson and Christian Huff reexamined their marriage after her mother, Korie Robertson, pointed out noticeable relationship struggles post-baby.

“My mom wrote us a letter that was a loving letter of, ‘Here’s what I see you’re struggling with, and here’s what I think could help you,’” Sadie, 29, exclusively told Us while discussing her new memoir, It’s Not Personal: Coming Face-to-Face With Who You Really Are. “Those things are hard to receive. First of all, you’re dealing with embarrassment. You’re like, ‘Oh my gosh, like, this is so embarrassing. She sees I’m struggling.’”

Sadie revealed in her new book that Korie, 53, delivered her and Christian, 28, a note during a family trip to New York City to promote Duck Dynasty: The Revival. (At the time, Sadie was newly postpartum after welcoming her third daughter, Kit, in August 2025.)

In addition to feeling embarrassment over Korie’s letter, Sadie wondered why she and Christian were being singled out after six years of marriage.

“You’re like, ‘Is everybody else getting a letter? Oh, it’s just us. OK, shoot. You know, we really are doing rough,’” the “Whoa That’s Good” podcaster, who also shares daughters Honey and Haven with Christian, recalled. “That was such a confronting thing, but yeah, that was the thing that really shifted things for our relationship because we just got honest about it.”

Sadie continued, “I think so many times in life you, kind of, accept that this is just the way it’s gonna be, and yet a life of faith calls you higher than that. It goes, ‘That’s not the way it’s just gonna be. There’s something better for you.’ And my mom was saying, ‘Hey, like, I see this in y’all. It doesn’t have to be that way, you know?’”

For Sadie and Christian, Korie’s letter “meant so much” because of her empathic tone.

“She was like, ‘I remember when your dad and I were at that stage, and I remember how it felt to be going through that,’” Sadie told Us, referring to her father, Willie Robertson. “Immediately just that empathy made me go, ‘Tell me more.’”

Sadie revealed that Korie shared “really helpful” lessons that she said “helped them in their season of little kids and this many years married and whatnot.”

“I think Christian and I have just gotten to a point in our communication that we’re just so open and honest with each other,” Sadie noted. “We are quick to be able to say, ‘OK, I missed it there, or I was being selfish there, or I need to be more more kind even when I’m tired,’ or whatever it is, whatever the silly thing is, just saying it, being quick to apologize, being quick to change and turn the corner. It’s helped us so much in our marriage. I will say that letter really kickstarted it for us.”

Reaching the other side of their marital issues, Sadie further paid tribute to Christian by dedicating It’s Not Personal to him.

“Christian is truly just an incredible human,” she gushed to Us. “Christian really is the most incredible, encouraging human. He is my best friend, he is the best girl dad in the world, he is so incredible. I feel like he doesn’t need everybody to tell him how awesome he is, but I’m his wife and I get to. I just wanted to dedicate the book to him because, so much of this message, he’s helped teach me by living it.”

Just as Sadie learned helpful lessons from her husband and her mom, she similarly hopes to pass down those pearls of wisdom to readers.

“I hope people feel that way with my writing [as I did from my mom’s letter], that, like, I know how it feels,” she said. “I’m feeling that too, but here’s how I’m overcoming it.”

In It’s Not Personal, Sadie shares candid stories and biblical citations to help readers reclaim what should be “personal.”

“It’s called It’s Not Personal, and just the response to the title has been so awesome because people get it. Everyone knows when that is thrown out, ‘it’s not personal,’ it is personal,” she explained. “It’s always personal, it feels personal, and my angle with that was really just a draw for people who have been afraid to step into faith, who are afraid of the confrontation of getting to know God and what that looks like.”

It’s Not Personal: Coming Face-to-Face With Who You Really Are is out now.

The Superman actor is a long time supporter of the foundation, having previously grown a mustache in support. This time, the actor is embracing his nerdy side as his latest team up pairs him with Google’s Antigravity (an AI tool on Googlebook) to create a 16-bit game called “Mustache Protocol.” In it, a suspiciously Cavill-looking mustachioed hero is making his mission to stop rogue CGI artists from erasing all the mustaches in the world. The actor post Part 2 (of a three part series) on his Instagram:

A post shared by Henry Cavill (@henrycavill)

As you can see, the hero has lots of muscles and a handlebar mustache very similar to the Witcher actor’s own fancy ‘stache. If you don’t, this is slightly poking fun at continuity errors in the movie, which yes, included disappearing pockets, but fans are here for the 'stache:

The actor is clearly having fun taking a break from several projects, including a Highlander reboot movie, and doing so for a worthy cause. Though I wasn’t surprised to see the style of the game had a delightful vintage feel to it. The stylistic choices really show off Cavill’s personality, and that’s why fans are loving the videos. Only he could make brisket feel like a reasonable health choice for a power up. Part of the joy in watching the actor create something so wholesome is seeing him show off his wonderfully geeky side, which fans get to see often. Surely the “game of the year awards” is Cavill’s for the taking, right?

Whether it’s his love of the Witcher video games or working with Amazon on the Warhammer 40,000 series, he’s never strayed from being just like the rest of us. He’s also reportedly attached to the Voltron live action adaptation of the animated series from the ‘80s. Though I have no information on whether or not he'll have a fancy 'stache.

I mustache you to remember that while you're supporting all of these projects, that you also check out the foundation's website and note the importance of the 'stache this Movember.
